key_insight: A combined homogenization and blunt-crack fracture model predicts how lattice fracture toughness changes from low to high relative density, with high-density failure increasingly governed by nodal stress concentrations and crack-tip geometry.
engineering_relevance: This work helps engineers design stronger lightweight lattices by tuning relative density, orientation, fillet radius, and base-material ductility to improve fracture resistance.
method: Analytical fracture model for triangular and hexagonal lattices
Homogenization + blunt-crack fracture theory across broad relative densities
Finite element simulations and laser-cut PMMA experiments for validation
evidence_signal: Finite element results and PMMA fracture experiments corroborate the analytical framework, including an observed ~1.6x toughness increase for quasi-brittle lattices over perfectly brittle ones.
watch_item: Brittle lattice failure is stochastic, especially at higher relative densities, so predictions may be sensitive to local crack path and specimen-specific geometry.
paper_title: Fracture of Lattice Materials from Low to High Relative Density
